verses.text: For the music director. A psalm by David. The heavens tell of God’s glory. The sky shows what his hands have made.
Day after day they pour out words, and night after night they reveal what they know.
There’s no speech or language where their voice goes unheard.
Their voice reaches across the earth, their words to the ends of the world. God has pitched a tent in the heavens for the sun,
which comes out like a groom leaving his room, like a strong runner eager to run the course.
It rises at one end of the heavens and makes its way to the other. Nothing escapes its heat.
The LORD’s instruction is perfect and restores the soul. His covenant is sure and gives wisdom to the inexperienced.
The LORD’s instructions are right and fill the heart with joy. His command is pure and gives light to the eyes.
The fear of the LORD is clean and lasts forever. His judgments are true and completely right.
They’re worth wanting more than gold, even piles of pure gold. They’re sweeter than honey straight from the comb.
They warn me, your servant. There’s great reward in keeping them.
Who can see all their own mistakes? Forgive the wrongs I don’t see.
Keep me, your servant, from sins I commit in defiance. Don’t let them rule over me. Then I’ll live uprightly, cleared of serious wrongdoing.
May the words I speak and the thoughts in my heart please you, LORD, my rock and my redeemer.
